column3: “Said to gather” is rendered “gave orders to gather,” and “sojourners” as “foreigners.”
“Iron to abundance” is rendered “large quantities of iron”; NASB supplies “to make,” and “there was no weight” is rendered “more … than could be weighed.”
“To there was no number” is rendered “beyond number.”
“A youth and weak” is rendered “young and inexperienced”; “to make great upward, for a name and for honor” is rendered “exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious.”
“It was with my heart” is rendered “I had intended.”
“Made” is rendered “waged,” and “the ground” as “the earth.”
“Here!” is rendered “Behold.” The Hebrew name “Solomon” is related to the word for peace.
“May he be” is rendered “be with you”; NASB supplies “that you may be.”
“Insight” is rendered “discretion,” and “appoint you over Israel” as “give you charge over Israel”; NASB supplies “so that you may.”
“Judgments” is rendered “ordinances,” and “on Israel” as “concerning Israel.”
“In my affliction” is rendered “with great pains.”
“Craftsmen of stone and wood” is rendered “masons of stone and carpenters.”
“There is no number” is rendered “there is no limit.”
“Your being” is rendered “your soul,” and “the articles of the holiness of God” as “the holy vessels of God.”
